events.title: Pirate scouts shadow a convoy
events.arrangement: Two small hulls pace the convoy from 140-160 wu, at the speed-revealed band edge - visible only to a player who is moving
events.startConditions: Convoy transits while pirate weight is nonzero; ambush encounter pre-stage
events.visibleCue: Two contacts holding EXACT convoy speed without joining it - honest traffic overtakes or falls behind; only a shadow paces

phases.name: pace
phases.visible: Shadows hold formation off the convoy's quarter, dark hulls, no strobes - the ABSENCE of signals is the signal

phases.name: probe
phases.visible: One shadow closes to 80 wu, counts the escort, drifts back out - a visible headcount

phases.name: decide
phases.visible: Either both break away (escort too strong - the convoy never knows how close it came) or they light drives and the existing ambush encounter fires

events.completion: Most runs end in the break-away: the player who noticed the shadows watched a robbery be priced and declined

interruptions.outcome: Immediate break-away; the convoy's escort visibly worked
Both flee or fight per existing pirate archetype

playerInterference: Warn the convoy by flying to it (proximity is the message)
Join the ambush when it fires
Hunt the scouts before they decide
events.criminalOpportunity: This IS the criminal opportunity, dramatized - and a player can do the same scouting arithmetic on any convoy
events.aftermath: If the ambush fires it runs the existing encounter with its loot/wreck outcomes
events.fallback: Convoy despawns: shadows break to sector edge and despawn
events.notes: Pre-stages the EXISTING ambush encounter with a visible reconnaissance act; the decline branch costs nothing and sells the world hardest.

events.title: Scavengers strip a fresh wreck before the law arrives
environment: wreck (class fresh - a recent kill, not an old field)
events.arrangement: Two small hulls at the wreck, working FAST, nose-in / nose-out alternating so one always faces the lane
events.startConditions: A fresh wreck exists (combat aftermath) with unclaimed salvage budget; no salvor assigned
events.visibleCue: Hulls at a wreck with NO salvage umbrellas - cutting light without confession light means the work is not licensed

phases.name: swoop
phases.visible: Both arrive fast and hard-stop at the wreck - salvors approach, scavengers pounce

phases.name: strip
phases.visible: Bare cut arcs, no hoods; pickups yanked aboard at double cadence; the lookout's nose never leaves the lane

phases.name: scatter
phases.visible: At a timer or a patrol contact both bolt in DIFFERENT directions - guilt has a geometry

events.completion: Wreck's easy salvage gone; scavengers vanish separately with partial loads

interruptions.outcome: Immediate scatter; dropped pickups spray behind the runners
Lookout paints you; if you keep closing they scatter (you might be law, and they never check)

playerInterference: Beat them to the wreck
Rob the robbers - their cradles are full and their guns are poor
Call it in by leading a patrol over (proximity chaining)
events.criminalOpportunity: The event is a tutorial: fresh wrecks pay best in the first two minutes, before anyone official arrives
events.aftermath: Wreck salvage budget visibly reduced; scattered pickups persist briefly
events.fallback: Wreck despawns: scavengers scatter immediately (their reason left)

events.title: Smuggler dead-drops a cache
environment: distinctive rock or lane-furniture marker away from lanes (the drop point wants a LANDMARK)
events.arrangement: Smuggler leaves the lane on a wide arc, passes the landmark at low speed WITHOUT stopping, and rejoins traffic elsewhere
events.startConditions: Smuggler-flagged trader with a hot manifest and patrol pressure in-sector
events.visibleCue: A trader flying a lane exit that serves no destination - the arc is smooth, unhurried and completely pointless unless you saw what fell

phases.name: drift_out
phases.visible: Casual lane exit, dim bar, nothing to see

phases.name: drop
phases.visible: One unlit pickup separates at the landmark - no strobe, no plume; you catch it by silhouette occlusion or not at all

phases.name: rejoin
phases.visible: Long arc back into traffic at a different bearing; the hull now flies honestly lighter

events.completion: Cache sits dark at the landmark; someone (ev_criminal_handoff, or a returning smuggler, or the player) collects it later

interruptions.outcome: No drop this pass; the smuggler orbits the sector and retries once

playerInterference: Take the cache (it is real contraband-class cargo)
Stake out the landmark for the pickup party
Sell the location by leading someone there
events.criminalOpportunity: The drop TEACHES the mechanic: quiet objects near landmarks are worth checking - and the player can run dead drops in reverse
events.aftermath: PERSISTENT cache pickup until claimed; a claimed cache spawns the collection visit within the session (chaining hook)
events.fallback: Smuggler killed before the drop: cargo spills at the kill site instead - the cache becomes a spill, same loot different story

events.title: Two criminals trade cargo far from witnesses
environment: empty quarter, ideally near a cold landmark; 200+ wu from stations and beats
events.arrangement: Both arrive from different bearings, park tail-to-tail 6 wu apart (guns facing OUT - the geometry of mutual distrust)
events.startConditions: A smuggler with cargo and a pirate with none in-sector; low patrol presence
events.visibleCue: Two hulls parked tail-to-tail in nowhere - honest transfers park parallel; only distrust parks back-to-back

phases.name: converge
phases.visible: Separate quiet approaches from opposite bearings, both dark

phases.name: standoff
phases.visible: Tail-to-tail hold; ten still seconds - the negotiation you cannot hear

phases.name: swap
phases.visible: Three pickups cross the gap one at a time, each fully landed before the next leaves - nobody extends credit out here

phases.name: part
phases.visible: Both depart on their arrival bearings reversed, never showing each other a stern

events.completion: Cargo changed hands off the books; both vanish into ordinary traffic

interruptions.outcome: Instant split, swap incomplete; remaining pickups drift at the site
Both bolt on diverging vectors; the pickups stay - evidence

playerInterference: Interrupt at pickup two of three and take the stranded piece
Destroy either party mid-swap for both loads
Just watch: you now know two hulls and one habit
events.criminalOpportunity: This is the fence mechanic performed in the open - the player learns handoffs exist, then finds them
events.aftermath: The receiving hull carries the cargo for the rest of its session run (scannable)
events.fallback: One party never arrives: the other waits 20 s, drops NOTHING, and leaves - a stood-up meet reads exactly like one

events.title: Raider hits an isolated miner
environment: field slot 250+ wu from the nearest patrol beat
events.arrangement: Raider approaches down the miner's blind cone (the working side - the one direction a cutting miner cannot watch)
events.startConditions: Miner in WORK at an isolated slot; pirate weight nonzero; existing ambush logic targeting a worker instead of a lane
events.visibleCue: A dark hull sliding into the dust plume behind a working miner - the cone that protects the work blinds the worker

phases.name: stalk
phases.visible: Raider drifts up the spall stream, closing unlit

phases.name: strike
phases.visible: One warning burst across the bow; miner's cone dies; both hold still - the stick-up frame

phases.name: toll
phases.visible: Miner jettisons part of its load (pickups); raider tractors them in while the miner sits dark

phases.name: leave
phases.visible: Raider departs; miner relights and either resumes or limps home short

events.completion: A robbery, not a murder: the region's ecology keeps its miner and the raider keeps its schedule - most runs end bloodless

interruptions.outcome: Existing combat; usually a wreck and a full spill

interruptions.trigger: Patrol or player closes during toll
interruptions.outcome: Raider bolts with whatever is already aboard

playerInterference: Intervene during stalk (the raider breaks off - hunts hate witnesses)
Take the jettisoned toll yourself mid-tractor - robbing the robber at his own stick-up
Escort miners you see working alone
events.criminalOpportunity: The toll pattern is reusable BY the player against any loaded worker - the event demonstrates the verb
events.aftermath: Tolled miner's next cycles run closer to the patrol ring (visible learned caution); the raider re-arms elsewhere
events.fallback: Miner despawns mid-toll: raider takes the drifting pickups and leaves - the scene still resolves
events.diagramMermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant R as Raider
  participant M as Miner
  R->>M: drifts up the spall stream (unlit)
  R->>M: warning burst across the bow
  M->>M: cone dies, holds still
  M-->>R: jettisons partial load
  R->>R: tractors pickups aboard
  R->>R: departs
  M->>M: relights, resumes or limps home

events.title: Pirate tug steals a disabled hull
environment: disabled hull (aftermath of ev_disabled_distress or combat)
events.arrangement: Tug arrives at a drifting disabled hull BEFORE the lawful responders, kisses on, and walks it toward the sector edge
events.startConditions: A disabled-ship state exists with the lawful recovery delayed (response timer lost the race)
events.visibleCue: A tug whose approach is right but whose HEADING is wrong - recovery walks hulls toward stations; theft walks them away

phases.name: claim_jump
phases.visible: Tug hard-docks the disabled hull, no floods, no apron courtesy

phases.name: walk_away
phases.visible: Pair moves at walking pace toward the boundary - the slowest getaway in crime, in full view

phases.name: vanish
phases.visible: Pair exits at the sector edge; the disabled crew's distress keeps flashing all the way out - the detail that makes it ugly

events.completion: Hull and cargo gone; the lawful tender arrives at empty space and sweeps it - a visible failure of the response system

interruptions.outcome: Tug drops the hull and bolts; recovery proceeds late but succeeds
Hull drifts free again, re-arming the lawful recovery event

playerInterference: Break the tow by killing the tug (the walk is 90 slow seconds of vulnerability)
Escort the theft for a cut (you are now a pirate)
Race to disabled hulls before EITHER side arrives
events.criminalOpportunity: The whole event IS one - and it prices the disabled-hull economy: whoever arrives first owns the outcome
events.aftermath: Stolen hulls seed the pirate nest's salvage stock (campaign pressure blip); saved hulls owe the region a story
events.fallback: Disabled hull despawns mid-walk: tug diverts to scavenge mode at the nearest wreck
events.notes: The 'tow' is the same parented-drift link as ev_tug_repositions_cargo - one link flag, two moralities.

events.title: Claim jumper works a staked rock
environment: rock carrying a claim mark (aftermath of ev_prospector_stakes_claim)
events.arrangement: Jumper cuts the STAKED rock; owner returns mid-theft; the argument is flown, not spoken
events.startConditions: A claimed rock exists with its owner absent (mid-cycle elsewhere)
events.visibleCue: A cut cone lighting a rock that carries someone else's lit stake - the two lights disagree and any pilot can read it

phases.name: poach
phases.visible: Jumper works the seam fast, positioned to keep the stake OUT of its own floodlight - even machines look guilty

phases.name: owner_returns
phases.visible: Owner arrives hot, then hard-stops 30 wu off and PAINTS the jumper - accusation by lamp

phases.name: push
phases.visible: Owner flies tightening orbits between jumper and rock, herding without firing; jumper's cone stutters - working under pressure

phases.name: yield_or_fight
phases.visible: Usually the jumper breaks off with a part load; sometimes it stands and the existing combat resolves it

events.completion: Owner resumes its rock, cutting closer to the stake than before - possession re-performed

interruptions.outcome: Both flee; the rock keeps its stake and its scar

playerInterference: Back the owner (herd alongside)
Back the jumper
Poach the rock YOURSELF while they argue - three-body crime
events.criminalOpportunity: Demonstrates that claims are enforced by presence, not law - absent owners lose ore, and the player owns a stake verb too
events.aftermath: Jumped claims lose yield; owners that win re-stake with a second mark (a double-marked rock is a story artifact)
events.fallback: Owner never returns: the jumper strips the rock and leaves; the orphaned stake stays as archaeology
events.notes: The brief's 'prospectors arguing through movement' - herding orbits are steering, the accusation is the existing PAINT reaction, and nobody speaks.

events.title: Pirates run a pop-up toll on a bend
environment: lane bend or diversion choke (composes with ev_lane_spot_closure's bulge)
events.arrangement: Two pirates flank the choke at 40 wu; traffic is stopped one hull at a time; a 'paid' hull passes while the next is held
events.startConditions: Existing toll encounter script; sited at a choke instead of open lane
events.visibleCue: Traffic STACKING at a bend - honest space never queues in the open, so a queue in nowhere means a hand is out

phases.name: setup
phases.visible: Pirates take flanking stations, running lights OFF then suddenly ON together - the gate declaring itself

phases.name: collect
phases.visible: Each held hull jettisons a token pickup and is waved past; the pile between the pirates grows - a visible till

phases.name: fold
phases.visible: At a patrol contact or quota both scoop the till and bolt on diverging vectors

events.completion: Gate folds before the law arrives; traffic unknots; the bend remembers nothing

interruptions.outcome: Existing toll-script violence branch; the queue scatters
Fold immediately; till pickups left drifting - free money with a story

playerInterference: Pay the toll (cheapest outcome)
Break the gate (two targets holding still)
Rob the TILL mid-collect - the pile is just pickups
events.criminalOpportunity: The till pile is the single richest unattended object in the region for ninety seconds
events.aftermath: Folded tolls re-site at a different choke next session window; the campaign pressure deck ticks
events.fallback: Both pirates lost: queue dissolves; till pickups persist
events.notes: The toll script exists; this stages it at a choke with the queue and the till made visible - the encounter's economy externalized into objects.
